subject: Dedicated throughput tiers — final review of thresholds + exclusions (reply by EOD Mon)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha_bello@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar_elsayed@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Dedicated throughput tiers — final review of thresholds + exclusions (reply by EOD Mon)

Hi all — we’re close to locking the Dedicated throughput tiers for beta. I need final sanity check / sign-off on (a) tier thresholds, (b) assumptions/exclusions, and (c) any “do not ship without” guardrails.

Docs:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PROD/Dedicated+throughput+SLO+PRD
- Measurement standard: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/Throughput+Measurement+Standard
- ADR-0127 (primary metric): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=ADR-0127
- ADR-0128 (tier/burst semantics): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=ADR-0128
- Shape catalog: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/INFRA/Dedicated+Hardware+Shapes+Catalog
- Tier matrix v1 (sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/tier-matrix-v1
- Bench baselines: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/dedicated-shapes-benchmark-results

What I’m proposing to publish (summary):
1) Primary SLI (Dedicated): sustained output tokens/sec, computed as a rate over a 5-min rolling window, per deployment_id, during “Serving” state. Objective expressed as p95 over the window meeting tier target.
2) Exclusions: warmup, scheduled maintenance window, customer-induced 4xx (invalid requests), and time spent in explicit “Overload/Throttling” mode (throttles are not breaches if policy is behaving as expected).
3) Tier semantics (names + behavior):
- Standard: best-effort burst; admission control kicks in earlier; SLO uses broader carve-outs; shape availability wide.
- Performance: higher sustained target; limited burst; stricter measurement windows; more aggressive alerting.
- Premium: highest sustained target; minimal burst but highest floor; limited regions/shapes; enhanced paging + tighter maintenance coordination.

Inline questions (please reply in-thread):
A) SRE: Are the exclusions / “throttling is expected behavior” language defensible + operationally measurable? Any wording that will create paging ambiguity?
B) Infra: Any tier->shape mapping that is unrealistic given Q1 supply? Regions we must explicitly exclude for Premium?
C) Runtime: Any concern that p95 output tps on 5-min rolling will be too noisy under mixed prompt sizes? If yes, propose an alternative we can ship now.

Goal: publish Confluence pages + provide Sales cheat-sheet on Tue (2/11). If something is a blocker, call it out explicitly.

Attachment: tier-matrix-v1-export.pdf (quick view of the sheet)

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference


From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Bello <aisha_bello@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar_elsayed@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 10:01 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput tiers — final review of thresholds + exclusions (reply by EOD Mon)

From SRE side, mostly yes. Two strong opinions:

1) “Time spent in Overload/Throttling mode excluded” needs very crisp definition + explicit customer-facing expectation. Otherwise we’ll get the “you throttled me so I never breach” argument.
   - I’d rather: throttling time is INCLUDED in SLI measurement, but throttling itself is not a breach if it is within the documented burst policy and we are still meeting the committed floor.
   - If we exclude throttling entirely, we need an upper bound on throttle ratio per tier (or we can’t reason about customer experience).

2) Scheduled maintenance carve-out: fine, but ensure we define the notification requirement (e.g., 72 hours for Premium, 24 hours for others) and cap it (e.g., X hours/month) so it doesn’t blow up trust.

If you want, Aisha and I can draft the wording in the SLO doc today and send for quick review.

— Rafa


From: Aisha Bello <aisha_bello@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar_elsayed@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 10:27 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput tiers — final review of thresholds + exclusions (reply by EOD Mon)

+1 to Rafa’s #1.

Operationally, we can measure:
- effective_output_tokens_per_second (rate)
- throttle_events / throttle_ratio
- queue_depth + saturation indicators

But “Serving state” needs to be tied to a control-plane signal (deployment health) not just runtime readiness, or we’ll argue later. Suggest language: “during periods when the deployment is Healthy and accepting traffic (excluding planned maintenance windows).”

On the p95 over 5-min rolling: ok as long as we also chart p50 so teams don’t optimize in the wrong direction. Alerts should be on burn (e.g., 30m fast burn + 6h slow burn) rather than raw p95 dips.

I’ll take an action to propose exact carve-out wording + alerting thresholds by tier and send back.

— Aisha


From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha_bello@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar_elsayed@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 11:08 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput tiers — final review of thresholds + exclusions (reply by EOD Mon)

Infra view:

- Premium tier: we should explicitly restrict initial availability to us-east-1 + us-west-2 only (maybe eu-west-1 if we get the next H100 tranche, but I would not publish that as GA).
- Shapes: I’m comfortable mapping Premium to H100 only for beta. Performance can be A100/H100. Standard can include L4 but we need to be careful about what “throughput guarantees” look like there; the variance is higher.
- MIG: Please do not advertise MIG for Premium; we can do no-MIG only. For Performance we can be flexible, but I’d prefer the tier page list “MIG not supported unless explicitly contracted.”

The other issue is “burst” promises. If Sales hears “burst,” they’ll sell it as “always can burst.” We need to position burst as “opportunistic if idle headroom exists,” with explicit caps.

If you want a crisp one-liner: Premium = predictable floor + constrained SKUs + strict admission control; Standard = wider SKUs + more variability + earlier throttling.

— Irene


From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha_bello@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar_elsayed@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 11:33 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput tiers — final review of thresholds + exclusions (reply by EOD Mon)

Agree w/ Irene.

Supply note: if we publish Premium “global” and then can’t deliver, it creates immediate exception pressure + churn risk. I’d rather be conservative and open regions over time.

Also: please add a note that shape availability is “subject to regional capacity” and that upgrades (Performance->Premium) may require lead time.

— Vanessa


From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Noah Patel <noah_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar_elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha_bello@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 12:22 PM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput tiers — final review of thresholds + exclusions (reply by EOD Mon)

Runtime thoughts:

- Metric choice: output tokens/sec is the right “physics” metric, but p95 over 5 minutes WILL be noisy if customers send mixed context lengths + streaming on/off mixed.
  - However: it’s shippable if we are explicit that the SLO assumes the tier’s published “workload profile” (prompt length distribution + max context) and we give customers a way to see when they’re out of profile.

- Exclusions: please keep warmup excluded (first N minutes after deploy/scale) and define N. We should align on 10 minutes after a rollout event, otherwise everyone argues.

- Throttling: I agree with Rafa. Throttling is our enforcement mechanism; it shouldn’t become a loophole. Better to define a “minimum admitted rate” (floor) and say requests above that may be throttled.

If you want a concrete text snippet: “Throughput guarantee applies to admitted requests within the published workload profile. Requests beyond the tier’s concurrency/burst policy may be throttled; throttling is not an SLA violation provided admitted traffic continues to meet the committed floor.”

— Sofia


From: Noah Patel <noah_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar_elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha_bello@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 2:38 PM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput tiers — final review of thresholds + exclusions (reply by EOD Mon)

+1 to Sofia.

One addition: Please avoid describing the objective as “p95 over 5-min rolling” without clarifying the aggregation order. People interpret this differently.

What we can compute consistently:
1) per deployment_id: compute 5-min rate = sum(output_tokens)/300s
2) then look at the distribution of that rate over the compliance period (e.g., monthly) and take p95

If we say that explicitly, it avoids the “p95 of p95” confusion.

Also, I’d strongly suggest we publish req/sec as a secondary diagnostic only (not committed), or we’ll get customers trying to convert between tokens and requests.

— Noah

(Omar pinged me separately: he’s aligned with the above; biggest ask is to ensure the docs call out streaming behavior and that streaming overhead can reduce effective tps at very low output lengths.)
